SourceTerm: 路逢達道人，不將語默對
CreatedBy: Codex Iriya construction lane C evidence-first

Senses.PreferredTarget: when meeting an accomplished person on the road, do not answer with speech or silence
AlternateTargets: meet an adept without responding verbally or silently
neither speech nor silence will answer an accomplished traveler
Senses.Note: Three quoted questions and one verse support “when meeting an accomplished person on the road, do not answer with speech or silence” across four independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：古人道：路逢達道人，不將語默對。未審將甚麼對？師曰：喫茶去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (五燈全書(第1卷-第33卷)). English Label: the unnamed monastic questioner quotes the maxim and asks what response remains; Xuefeng sends him to drink tea.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The 問 frame assigns the maxim-bearing question to an unnamed monastic; 師曰 or 師云 begins the named teacher's reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：路逢達道人，不將語默對。未審將甚麼對？師曰：瞥爾三千界。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1568.xml). Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)). Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州因僧問：路逢達道人，不將語默對。未審將甚麼對？師曰：人從陳州來，不得許州信。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Lineage Mirror and Grove (宗鑑法林). English Label: the unnamed monastic questioner asks Zhaozhou how to meet the maxim; Zhaozhou answers with a traveler who brings no news from the neighboring prefecture.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪竇顯頌：問曾不知，答還不會，月冷風高，古巖寒檜。堪笑路逢達道人，不將語默對
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X83/X83n1578.xml). Record of Pointing at the Moon (指月錄). English Label: Xuedou Chongxian includes the maxim in a verse that first says the question did not know and the answer still did not understand.

Senses.Explanation: When meeting an accomplished person on the road, do not answer with speech or silence states its prohibition through the paired objects speech and silence. Three unnamed monastics quote it and ask what to use instead; Xuefeng answers 'drink tea,' Shoushan says it flashes through the three-thousandfold world, and Zhaozhou speaks of a traveler without neighboring news. Xuedou's verse quotes the same line after saying that neither question nor answer understood.
